::: {#exr-01-science-and-pseudo-science-interactive}
## Science and pseudo-science, interactive

Drag each mark to the side it belongs to. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "sci",
   "label": "Science"
  },
  {
   "id": "pseudo",
   "label": "Pseudo-science"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "Revises its claims when evidence contradicts them",
   "b": "sci"
  },
  {
   "t": "Makes risky, checkable predictions",
   "b": "sci"
  },
  {
   "t": "States its own limits and uncertainty",
   "b": "sci"
  },
  {
   "t": "Immune to evidence — always the same answer",
   "b": "pseudo"
  },
  {
   "t": "Explains everything after the fact",
   "b": "pseudo"
  },
  {
   "t": "Claims certainty",
   "b": "pseudo"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "The distinguishing mark of science is not being right but changing in response to evidence.",
 "ref": "sec-01-what-research-is",
 "reflabel": "What research is"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-01-the-information-supply-chain-interactive}
## The information supply chain, interactive

Click the stations of the supply chain in order, from where a finding is produced to where most claims reach us. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="order">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "steps": [
  "Original studies",
  "Syntheses",
  "Professional layer",
  "Media",
  "Feeds"
 ],
 "explain": "Reach and speed increase along the chain; quality control and detail decrease. The task is to trace a claim back to the left.",
 "ref": "sec-01-what-research-is",
 "reflabel": "Three claims and one question",
 "hint": "click the stations, from original studies to feeds"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-01-the-three-conditions-of-research-interactive}
## The three conditions of research, interactive

Select the conditions that the working definition of research requires. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="pick">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "options": [
  {
   "t": "An original contribution",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "A systematic process",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "Openness to criticism",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "A large sample",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "A positive result",
   "ok": false
  },
  {
   "t": "A vendor sponsor",
   "ok": false
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Remove any one of the three conditions and what remains is no longer research: a penetration-test report, for instance, is systematic and documented but rarely original.",
 "ref": "sec-01-what-research-is",
 "reflabel": "A working definition"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-01-development-project-or-research-project-interactive}
## Development project or research project?, interactive

The same project, twice: sort each statement to the version it describes. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "dev",
   "label": "Development project"
  },
  {
   "id": "res",
   "label": "Research project"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "We build a password-manager onboarding flow for the client",
   "b": "dev"
  },
  {
   "t": "We build the flow — and investigate where users abort, and why",
   "b": "res"
  },
  {
   "t": "Success = it ships and works",
   "b": "dev"
  },
  {
   "t": "Success = it ships and we can say something new and evidenced about drop-off",
   "b": "res"
  },
  {
   "t": "Report: what we built and how",
   "b": "dev"
  },
  {
   "t": "Report: what we built, how we studied it, what we found, what it means beyond this client",
   "b": "res"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "The research version is more useful to the client, not less, because it explains why the numbers move.",
 "ref": "sec-01-reading-material",
 "reflabel": "Reading material"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::

::: {#exr-01-what-research-is-not-interactive}
## What research is not, interactive

Which of these, on its own, is not research? Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="pick">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "options": [
  {
   "t": "\"I built a tool and it works\"",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "\"I searched the web and summarised\"",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "\"Our penetration test found 12 vulnerabilities\"",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "\"Everyone on the team agrees\"",
   "ok": true
  },
  {
   "t": "A systematic study whose method and findings others can evaluate",
   "ok": false
  }
 ],
 "explain": "A tool without a question, a summary of opinions, a client report and a consensus each lack at least one of the three conditions.",
 "ref": "sec-01-worked-examples-and-tables",
 "reflabel": "What research is not"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::
